saigon.name: The Cafe Apartment
saigon.why: An old apartment block on Nguyen Hue with a different café in almost every flat, lit up floor by floor at night.

saigon.name: Tan Dinh pink church
saigon.why: A bubblegum-pink 1870s church; the classic Saigon photo.

saigon.name: Nguyen Hue walking street
saigon.why: Saigon's big pedestrian boulevard, busy with music and lights after dark.

saigon.name: Saigon Central Post Office
saigon.why: French colonial hall with painted maps and a big portrait of Ho Chi Minh.

saigon.name: Thien Hau Temple
saigon.why: Giant spiral incense coils hanging from the roof, filling the temple with smoke and light.
saigon.what: Cholon: Thien Hau Temple and Binh Tay Market

saigon.name: Banh Mi Huynh Hoa
saigon.why: Saigon's most famous banh mi, stuffed thick with pork and pâté.

saigon.name: Ben Thanh Market
saigon.why: The big central market; the night market sets up outside at dusk.

saigon.name: Cu Chi Tunnels
saigon.why: Crawling the wartime tunnels and the tiny hidden trapdoor.

saigon.name: Bui Vien walking street
saigon.why: The neon backpacker street with bars spilling onto the road and loud music.
saigon.note: Not in the plan: loud and boozy late at night. A 10-minute walk from a District 1 hotel for a quick look any evening.

saigon.name: Landmark 81 SkyView
saigon.why: Glass-floored viewing deck at the top of Vietnam's tallest tower.
saigon.note: Not in the plan: about A$30 each, and the rooftop bar on 19 Dec has a similar view.

phuquoc.name: Kiss Bridge
phuquoc.why: Two halves of a bridge that almost meet over the sea; couples kiss at the gap at sunset.

phuquoc.name: Kiss of the Sea show
phuquoc.why: Night show on the water with fountains, lasers and fireworks.

phuquoc.name: Sao Beach
phuquoc.why: Powder-white sand and calm, clear water.

phuquoc.name: Grand World
phuquoc.why: A mini-Venice of canals, gondolas and colourful buildings.

phuquoc.name: Starfish Beach
phuquoc.why: Shallow water with starfish on the sand.

phuquoc.name: Dinh Cau night market
phuquoc.why: Seafood grilled to order by the harbour.

phuquoc.name: Ham Ninh fishing village
phuquoc.why: Stilt houses and a long wooden pier out over the sea.

phuquoc.name: Hon Thom cable car
phuquoc.why: One of the world's longest sea cable cars, 7.9 km over the islands.
phuquoc.note: Not in the plan: about A$40–50 each. Would fit the free morning on 25 Dec.

bangkok.name: Grand Palace and the Emerald Buddha
bangkok.why: Gold-covered spires and the country's most sacred temple.
bangkok.what: Grand Palace and Wat Phra Kaew

bangkok.name: Wat Arun
bangkok.why: The porcelain-covered riverside temple, best from across the river at dusk.

bangkok.name: Mae Klong Railway Market
bangkok.why: Stalls fold back seconds before a train creeps through the market.

bangkok.name: Jodd Fairs
bangkok.why: The most-filmed night market, with the giant volcano pork ribs.

bangkok.name: Chinatown (Yaowarat)
bangkok.why: Neon signs and street food on Yaowarat Road after dark.

bangkok.name: Wat Paknam
bangkok.why: A glass pagoda with a jade Buddha under a ceiling painted with the universe.

bangkok.name: ICONSIAM
bangkok.why: Riverside mega-mall with an indoor floating market; NYE fireworks out front.

bangkok.name: Talat Noi
bangkok.why: Old riverside lanes with street art, crumbling shophouses and stacks of car parts.

bangkok.name: Chatuchak Weekend Market
bangkok.why: Over 10,000 stalls; coconut ice cream and vintage finds.

bangkok.name: Golden Mount
bangkok.why: Golden chedi on a hill with a view over the old city at sunset.

bangkok.name: Lumphini Park lizards
bangkok.why: Huge monitor lizards wandering around the lakes.

bangkok.name: Amphawa fireflies
bangkok.why: Long-tail boats along the canals to see fireflies in the trees.

bangkok.name: Mahanakhon SkyWalk
bangkok.why: A glass floor 314 m above the city.
bangkok.note: Not in the plan: about A$45 each, and Three Sixty on 30 Dec covers the sunset view.

bangkok.name: Jay Fai
bangkok.why: The Michelin-starred street-food cook in ski goggles, famous for her crab omelette.
bangkok.note: Not in the plan: queues of 2–4 hours and about A$50 a dish.
